chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ibn Abi Najran from Safwan ibn Yahya from 'Isa ibn al-Qasim said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had intercourse with a woman and kissed her, provided that he had not fully penetrated her, and then he married her daughter. He said: 'If he had not fully penetrated the mother, there is no harm (in marrying the daughter), and if he had fully penetrated her, he should not marry (the daughter).'

key_terms.بَاشَرَ: To have sexual intercourse or engage in foreplay
key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ: There is no harm / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to marry a woman's daughter if her father had sexual intercourse with her mother but did not fully penetrate her?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific condition of *khalwah* (seclusion) and consummation in determining the prohibition of marriage between a man and his former partner's daughter. While the general rule prohibits marrying the daughter of one's wife, this hadith distinguishes that mere intimacy without full penetration does not create the same barrier, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on actual consummation (*idkhal*) as the decisive factor for permanent prohibition.
